subject: general
question: Who is the composer of treatise of music Brihaddesi?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Matanga**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Matanga Muni**, a legendary musicologist, is the author of the seminal Sanskrit treatise **Brihaddesi**, composed approximately between the **6th and 9th centuries AD**.
 
• The **Brihaddesi** serves as a vital bridge between the ancient music (**Gandharva**) described by **Bharata Muni** in the **Natya Shastra** and the medieval evolution of Indian classical music.
 
• This work is historically significant for being the first to provide a formal definition of the term **Raga**. **Matanga** defines it as a combination of notes that "colors" or "delights" the minds of listeners.
 
• In this treatise, **Matanga** introduced the concept of **Desi Sangeet** (regional music) and **Marga Sangeet** (classical/celestial music), acknowledging for the first time the importance of folk and regional melodies in the classical tradition.
 
• The text also discusses the **Srutis** (microtones), the **Swaras** (notes), and the **Grama** system (the ancient scale systems of **Shadja-grama** and **Madhyama-grama**).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Sharangadeva (13th Century)**:

 
 
• He was the author of the **Sangita Ratnakara**, which is arguably the most influential work in the history of Indian musicology.
 
• He served in the court of **King Singhana II** of the **Yadava Dynasty** in **Devagiri** (Maharashtra).
 
• His work is often called the **Saptadhyayi** because it consists of **seven chapters** covering everything from sound production to dance and rhythm.
 
 
 
• **Haripala (14th Century)**:
 
 
• **Haripala**, a king of the **Chaulukya Dynasty** in **Gujarat**, authored the treatise **Sangita Sudhakara**.
 
• He is credited with being one of the first scholars to explicitly categorize Indian music into two distinct traditions: **Hindustani Sangeet** (Northern) and **Carnatic Sangeet** (Southern).
 
 
 
• **Ramamatya (16th Century)**:
 
 
• He was a prominent musicologist in the **Vijayanagara Empire** during the reign of **Aliya Rama Raya**.
 
• He wrote the **Svaramelakalanidhi** around **1550 AD**, which laid the conceptual groundwork for the modern **Mela** (parent scale) system used in **Carnatic music** today.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Definition of Desi**: In **Brihaddesi**, **Matanga** explains that music which is performed by **common people** (women, children, and cowherds) in different **Deshas** (regions) for pleasure is known as **Desi**.
 
• **Evolution of Instruments**: **Matanga** provided detailed descriptions of the **Veena** (stringed instruments) and discussed the **Kinnari Veena**, contributing to the development of instrumental music theory.
 
• **Prabandha**: The treatise contains early descriptions of the **Prabandha** form, which were structured musical compositions that preceded modern forms like **Dhrupad** and **Kriti**.
 
• **Legacy**: While large portions of the original **Brihaddesi** have been lost over **centuries**, the surviving fragments remain the primary source for understanding the transition of Indian music into the **Raga** system.
